emails.single_idea: Resend is now available as a separate platform for event-driven transactional email; for engineers running into built-in sender limits, the material difference is that paid Resend plans have no daily email limit.
unresolved: Unresolved strategy/material gap: The supplied material does not establish how Resend connects to Supabase Auth—custom SMTP versus application/API changes—or provide a setup resource where the reader can assess compatibility and effort before creating an account.

After "Resend does not change the auth platform’s own rate-limit setting," add the specific Supabase dashboard setting that must be changed and clarify whether Resend has any separate per-second or monthly limits.

Context (grounded; applicability must be checked): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.

assets.title: Send auth email with Resend
assets.content:
Subject: Send auth email with Resend
Preview text: Evaluate a separate sending platform with clear daily limits.

Give auth email a separate sending path

Hi there,

Resend is now available as a separate platform for sending personalized, event-driven transactional email from your own verified domain.

If a hosted auth provider’s built-in sender constrains signup confirmations, password resets, invitations, or OTPs, you can evaluate Resend independently using a Resend API key.

The limits are explicit: the Free plan allows 100 emails per day. Pro, Scale, and Enterprise plans have no daily email limit, so moving to a paid plan does not exchange one daily cap for another.

Resend does not change the auth platform’s own rate-limit setting. After configuring a separate sender, that setting still needs to be adjusted in the platform’s dashboard.

Create a free account to begin setup with your verified domain and API key.

Sign up for free →

- the Resend team

assets.content:
Subject: Test Resend without real recipients
Preview text: Simulate delivery, bounce, and complaint events before configuring a production route.

Test the email event path before production

Hi there,

A provider evaluation should not require sending test messages to real people. Resend provides test addresses that simulate delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events without affecting your domain reputation.

Resend is now available as an email sending platform for developers, connecting application-triggered messages through SMTP or official SDKs.

Send to delivered@resend.dev, bounced@resend.dev, and complained@resend.dev. These simulations let you exercise Resend’s Dashboard, Webhooks, and API together before configuring a real transactional-email route.

The Free plan allows 100 transactional emails per day and 3,000 per month. Check that boundary against expected authentication and notification volume before investing setup time.

This test does not validate production deliverability, production volume, or your hosted authentication platform’s SMTP and rate-limit configuration. It gives you a bounded way to inspect the event path first.

Get started →

- the Resend team
